To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) EPAs are units of measure that describe a particular profession’s unique abilities and responsibilities; 2) EPAs can be implemented in pharmacy education to link individual competencies for a student’s progression; and 3) EPAs can serve as a mechanism for pharmacy faculty to assess a student’s progression using a levels of decreasing supervision.

the use of EPAs in the pharmacy curriculum has the potential to improve the quality of the pharmacy curriculum, enhance the student learning experience, and provide a mechanism for assessing student progression.

the implementation of EPAs within the pharmacy curriculum has the potential to improve the quality of pharmacy education by better aligning the educational process with the practice setting and to improve the assessment of students’ abilities.

the following: the development of a framework for a novel approach to the design, delivery and evaluation of pharmacy education, which is underpinned by the use of EPAs; the development of a set of pharmacy EPAs; the implementation of EPAs within the curriculum and the assessment of student progress; and the use of EPA-based assessment in the evaluation of pharmacy education.

the use of EPAs in pharmacy education is a novel and exciting concept, but it requires a significant time investment and a willingness to embrace the change in culture.
